blocks.md: This lesson follows **Credit Across Turns** in *Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards, § Credit Across Turns
blocks.md: In the connection-pool repair, an agent might run the failing reproducer, read `src/pool.py`, and correctly identify the missed notification on connection return, only to introduce a syntax error in its final edit. A verifier that evaluates only the end state marks the entire trajectory as failed, exposing the multi-turn credit-assignment problem introduced in a later section: that terminal failure characterizes the trajectory as a whole, not whether the earlier diagnosis was a mistake.

questions.q: The section **Credit Across Turns** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A terminal reward gives every turn the same reward-to-go, so separating a useful step from a faulty one is bought with a critic, more samples, or step-level signals, each at its own cost.
Agent RL throughput is set by the rollout loop, not the gradient step, so the serial slot cycle caps capacity and Amdahl's law bounds any single-stage speedup.
Ratios and gradients are valid only on per-invocation records of the delivered prefix token IDs, sampled token IDs, and behavior log probabilities under the actual sampling transforms.

A group whose rewards all tie carries no reward gradient, occurring with probability p^G + (1-p)^G, so the rollout cost of one informative group is G/C and difficulty targeting toward p near 0.5 lowers it.
